column3: Close to the Greek; “authority” is rendered “power.”

NKJV adds “Assuredly, I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah … than for that city,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks this sentence and reads “whatever place will not receive you.”
NKJV has “he said,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “they were saying.”
NKJV has “or like one of the prophets,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “a prophet like one of the prophets.”
NKJV has “This is John … he has been raised from the dead!,” following the Textus Receptus wording; the critical text reads “John, whom I beheaded, has been raised.”
NKJV has “he did many things,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “he was greatly perplexed.”
NKJV has “Herodias' daughter herself,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “his daughter Herodias.”
